checked.found: Searched: fossils dated about 6 to 7 million years ago (faunal dating); 2022 Nature study argues bipedal features, though the femur is disputed. Description is hedged with 'may be'; the name states upright walking more firmly than the evidence, but is acceptable.
Searched: Tugen Hills, Kenya fossils dated 5.8 to 6.1 million years ago; femur analysis indicates habitual bipedalism.
Searched: Ardi, Ethiopia, 4.4 million years ago (4.32 to 4.51); grasping feet, climbed and walked upright, woodland habitat.
Searched: earliest known australopith, about 4.2 million years ago (range 4.3 to 3.8) around Lake Turkana, Kenya.
Searched: Laetoli trackways in volcanic ash, Tanzania, about 3.66 million years ago; earliest unequivocal evidence of bipedalism.
Searched: conventional range 3 to 2 million years ago (Australian Museum says 3.2 to 2); newer Sterkfontein dating argues up to 3.7 million. 3.0 is a defensible start.
Searched: Gona, Ethiopia tools 2.6 to 2.5 million years ago, the oldest known Oldowan.
Searched: P. boisei lived in East Africa 2.3 to 1.2 million years ago; 'Nutcracker Man' for its huge molars (diet debated, but description says 'tough plants').

Searched: earliest Homo erectus about 1.9 to 2.0 million years ago; longer legs, shorter arms, larger body; a 2020 study says the ribcage was Neanderthal-like, but 'modern body proportions' is the standard summary.

Searched: Dmanisi is about 1.8 million years old and the oldest human skeletal remains outside Africa, but Shangchen, China stone tools are dated about 2.12 million years, so 'oldest known people outside Africa' is contested.
checked.suggestion: Small-brained early humans settled at Dmanisi in the Caucasus, among the oldest known people outside Africa.

checked.found: Searched: Sima del Elefante jaw (ATE9-1) with flints, dated 1.2 to 1.1 million years ago (a later find may be about 1.4); species assignment to H. antecessor is provisional.
Searched: 2012 PNAS study, burned plant ash and bone about 1 million years ago, deep in the cave; a later claim pushes older but is less established.
Searched: Neanderthal-like traits in Europe at least 400,000 years ago; estimates range 200,000 to 400,000+, and origin region is debated.
Searched: Rising Star fossils 335,000 to 236,000 years old, curved finger bones, brain 465 to 610 cc; dates cover only sampled fossils.
Searched: Jebel Irhoud, Morocco, about 300,000 years ago, oldest securely dated Homo sapiens.
Searched: Misliya upper jaw fragment with teeth, Mount Carmel, Israel, 177,000 to 194,000 years old.
Searched: Xiahe jaw minimum age 160,000 years, same as oldest Denisova Cave material; Denisovans known from teeth, a finger bone and jaw.
Searched: Rizal et al. 2019, Ngandong last appearance 117,000 to 108,000 years ago; earliest end of window used.
Searched: Liang Bua individuals about 1.06 to 1.1 m tall (not knee-high); skeletal remains 100,000 to 60,000 years old, so the year is fine.
checked.suggestion: A metre-tall human with a tiny brain lived on an Indonesian island, hunting dwarf elephants and making stone tools.

checked.found: Searched: 2019 Nature study, Callao Cave, Luzon; minimum ages 50,000 and 67,000 years; curved toe bone.
Searched: December 2024 Nature and Science studies place the main interbreeding about 50,500 to 43,500 years ago; about 2% Neanderthal DNA in non-Africans.
Searched: Iberian disappearance estimates range about 45,000 to 37,000 years ago; about 40,000 is within range.
